title: SOP: Troubleshooting and Recovering an Unresponsive Unix Server
summary: This article provides the standard operating procedure for responding to a Unix server that is reported as down and inaccessible. It covers initial network triage, out-of-band console access, and system recovery to restore operating system functionality.
symptoms: Server does not respond to ICMP ping requests
SSH connections time out or are actively refused
Applications hosted on the Unix machine are unreachable
rootCause: An unresponsive Unix machine can be caused by a variety of system-level issues, including a kernel panic, hardware failure, network interface disconnection, or resource exhaustion (such as an Out-Of-Memory condition freezing the OS).
resolutionSteps: Step 1: Verify network connectivity by performing a ping and traceroute to the server's IP address to rule out intermediate network routing issues.
Step 2: Log in to the Out-of-Band (OOB) management interface (e.g., iLO, iDRAC, or VMware vSphere Web Client) to view the virtual or physical console for on-screen errors like a kernel panic.
Step 3: Attempt to log in via the console. If the system is completely frozen, initiate a graceful restart via the OOB power controls. If graceful restart fails, perform a hard reset.
Step 4: Once the server is back online, SSH into the machine and review system logs (e.g., /var/log/messages, /var/log/syslog, or dmesg) to identify and remediate the underlying cause of the outage.
